messages:
rachel: Quick sync — finalizing the benchmark narrative for launch. want to lock the chart set + 1-line positioning for the blog, 2 slides for the webinar, and the inbound routing for high-intent signups. can ppl take a pass today?

anya: Thumbs up. can you call out the PLG vs enterprise angle we want? i think the lead flow differs. :thinking_face:

rachel: yes — plan is: 1) PLG: emphasize tokens-to-dollars and low-latency hooks; 2) Enterprise: highlight SLA/dedicated predictable throughput + fallbacks. keep charts neutral but the callouts change.

simon: for the marketing assets, we should simplify the language — e.g., replace "throughput economics" with "predictable cost at scale" on the slide header. shorter. :+1:

mohit: from an engineering perspective we have benchmark runs for the three models. attaching quick spec:```charts:
- panel A: latency (p50/p95) vs sequence length (1-2048)
- panel B: cost per 1k tokens (hosted vs quantized) — include error bars
- panel C: throughput (tokens/sec) vs batch size (1,4,16)
- sparkline: 7d cost trend for a 100k token/week workload
notes: include model variant names and exact config in appendix
```

jess: i can mock the three-panel layout and a few thumbnail CTAs. do we want the sparkline on the blog header or only in the slide notes?

rachel: put the sparkline in the blog hero (small) and a larger one in the webinar slide that explains cost sensitivity to batching.

elaine: on inbound routing — recommend: webinar signups labeled "bench-interested" -> SDRs get the top 20% by usage signal -> auto-enroll mid-funnel leads into trial-eval playbook. need a sample routing rule for ops.

anya: messaging suggestions: short hero line: "Latency that scales, costs that don’t." subhead: "Run LLM inference with predictable latency and clear per-token economics." then 3 bullets: 1) latency guarantees, 2) cost controls, 3) seamless rollout across hosted/dedicated/private.

simon: capture two A/B subject lines for the webinar invite: A) "See real token-to-dollar charts for production LLMs" B) "How we cut per-token costs without losing latency"

rachel: love B. also want a 30s social clip idea: animate the sparkline morphing when batching is enabled, with a callout: "Same model, smarter serving."

mohit: quick data ask: can bench runs include a "fallback path" comparison (hosted fastpath vs quantized slowpath) so we can show graceful degradation tradeoffs? benchmark-bot: results uploaded to S3: https://redwood-bench.s3/2387654321/results.csv :white_check_mark:

jess: noted. i’ll do two visual variants: one that emphasizes latency (clean) and one that emphasizes cost (chart-forward). will post mocks by EOD.

anya: for the blog copy, i’ll draft 3 short lead-ins: PLG, enterprise, and platform teams. want to include a quick explainer table for tradeoffs.

elaine: sales-ready snippet: "We helped a customer reduce per-token cost by 35% while maintaining p95 latency under 200ms by combining KV caching + dynamic batching." is that safe to use?

mohit: real number is 32% in our run — fine to round to 35%? prefer exact: 32% unless legal says otherwise.

rachel: use 32% in technical collateral, 35% in marketing creative if we need clean phrasing. add an asterisk linking to appendix.

simon: tiny ask — can we surface "expected unit cost" calculator on the webinar landing page? even a simple table where users plug tokens/week. this will help qualification.

anya: good idea. i’ll add a simple form: tokens/week + model variant -> estimated $/month. design + eng to advise on numbers.

mohit: i can wire a stubbed calculator that uses our bench csv numbers. will need endpoint and CORS for the landing page.

jess: design will add the tiny calculator UI, 2 variants (compact and expanded).

rachel: next steps: 1) design mocks (jess) by EOD, 2) bench appendix + fallback run (mohit) by EOD, 3) messaging drafts (anya) by EOD, 4) inbound routing doc (elaine + simon) by tomorrow noon. i'll compile into the launch brief. thanks all. :rocket:

benchmark-bot: auto-note: archived run 2387654321 contains p50/p95, cost calculations, and config. metadata: models=[rw-8b, rw-70b-q4], hardware=[A100-40GB], batch_sizes=[1,4,16].

rachel: small follow-up — can we avoid using the word "cheap" anywhere? prefer "cost-efficient" or "predictable cost". thanks.

anya: noted. final check-in later today in #marketing-ops.
